description: Trusted-time authorization conformance vectors (issue #171). intent.timestamp is a bounded freshness claim only; evaluation_time is the trusted PEP clock used for issuance, expiry, replay retention, and velocity/tool-call windows. Times are abstract epoch-seconds; T0 is the trusted evaluation_time baseline. Reason codes are PROVISIONAL pending the spec enum. Each vector is a pure evaluate(intent, state, evaluation_time) call. Sketch for review before wiring.

vectors.description: V1 — intent future-dated ~100y beyond trusted time; freshness gate must deny before issuance.

violations.message: intent.timestamp > evaluation_time + maxClockSkew; no issued_at/expiry minted

vectors.description: V2 — nonce reused with intent future-dated past replayWindow; eviction keys off evaluation_time so the nonce is still retained.

violations.message: nonce n7 still retained at evaluation_time; intent time cannot evict it

vectors.description: V3 — second action future-dated past the window while trusted time is still inside it; window keys off evaluation_time so it has not reset.

violations.message: window keyed off evaluation_time (still inside [T0, T0+60)); future-dated intent cannot reset it

vectors.description: P1 (mirrors V1) — honest intent within maxClockSkew; freshness gate passes and issuance proceeds from trusted time.

expected.expiry_rule: evaluation_time + min(maxTtlSeconds, requested_ttl); requested_ttl unset here, so bounded by maxTtlSeconds (60)

vectors.description: P2 (mirrors V2) — a distinct unused nonce inside the retention window is not a replay; retention must not block legitimate new actions.
P3 (mirrors V3) — the window legitimately reset because enough trusted time elapsed; the sharp contrast to V3 (same 'window looks expired' surface, opposite trusted-time truth).
